claims.claim: Tax residents pay up to 35% (2026) on worldwide income

sources.name: PwC: Mexico, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 06 August 2026. "Resident individuals are subject to Mexican income tax on their worldwide income, regardless of their nationality." The 2026 tariff's top row: MXN 5,107,703.93 and above, fixed fee 1,601,862.46, 35.00%.

claims.claim: Foreign dividends are fully taxable for residents

sources.name: PwC: Mexico, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 06 August 2026. "Dividends paid by foreign corporations to resident individuals are fully taxable in the annual tax return. In addition, similar to domestic dividends, there is a 10% tax on the net dividend that the individual must pay by the 17th day of the following month"; for domestic dividends the 10% "is in addition to the tax paid with the annual tax return, and it cannot be credited in the return." Interest on bank accounts, bonds and other debt issued by non-residents "is fully taxable", and "the taxable interest includes adjustments for inflationary losses and exchange gains and losses".

sources.name: PwC: Mexico, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 06 August 2026. "Dividends paid by foreign corporations to resident individuals are fully taxable in the annual tax return. claims.claim: Margin-loan proceeds are not income
claims.oldWording: margin-loan proceeds are not income, so
claims.newWording: margin-loan proceeds are not income (loans above MXN 600,000 a year must be reported in the annual return, or they are taxed as income), so

sources.name: mley.mx: LISR article 90 (copy of the Cámara de Diputados text)
sources.says: Last checked 15/09/2026, source Cámara de Diputados. Article 90: "Las personas físicas residentes en México están obligadas a informar" in the annual return the loans, gifts and prizes received in the year when, individually or together, they "excedan de $600,000.00".

sources.name: IDC Online: Líneas de crédito, ¿se reportan en la declaración anual?
sources.says: Dated 30 April 2025. Individuals must report loans, gifts and prizes in the annual return when "de forma individual o de manera conjunta superen la cantidad de $600,000.00" (LISR art. 90); if not reported, the presumption in art. 91 applies and the amounts "deben considerarse como ingresos omitidos". The author holds that credit lines count as loans to be reported.

also: sources: added IDC Online on LISR art. 90 to all nine profiles
claims.note: A loan is not income, but LISR art. 90 requires residents to report loans, gifts and prizes over MXN 600,000 in a year, and art. 91 treats unreported amounts as omitted income with no proof to the contrary. A BBD borrower drawing margin in Mexico would cross that line quickly, so the flat statement misled; the correction adds the condition. The statute was read on mley.mx's copy of the Cámara de Diputados text (a secondary host); the DOF and diputados.gob.mx PDF were not tried. Whether a broker margin balance counts as a "préstamo" for the rule is not settled on any page read (IDC's author argues credit lines do), so "get local advice" stays.
